one_liner: Team messaging platform with channels, DMs, huddles, canvases, lists and workflow automation.
auth_notes: OAuth v2 (oauth.v2.access) returns xoxb bot tokens and, via user_scope, user tokens under authed_user; tokens do not expire unless revoked. A v2_user flow (oauth/v2_user/authorize + oauth.v2.user.access) is recommended for MCP/desktop clients. redirect_uri must be HTTPS; scopes are additive and cannot be downgraded; PKCE only mentioned for desktop MCP clients.
access_notes: Credentials are free and self-serve (free workspace or free Slack Developer Program basic sandbox). But commercially distributed apps not listed in the Slack Marketplace (which requires review) have conversations.history/conversations.replies cut to Tier 1 (1 req/min, max 15 objects) since 29 May 2025; internal customer-built apps and Marketplace apps are exempt. The Slack-hosted MCP server is restricted to Marketplace-published or internal apps (unlisted apps prohibited). Workspace admins can require app approval.
api_breadth_notes: ~360 Web API methods: admin.* (~135), conversations.* (~28), apps.* (~23), files.* (~15), chat.* (~13), users.* (~13), slackLists.* (~12), plus canvases, reactions, reminders, search, views, workflows, etc.
mcp_notes: Slack-hosted remote MCP at https://mcp.slack.com/mcp (Streamable HTTP, JSON-RPC; no SSE, no Dynamic Client Registration). Confidential OAuth with the app's client_id/secret; user tokens via oauth/v2_user. Tools: search messages/files/users/channels, read channels/threads, send/schedule/draft messages, create channels, reactions, canvases, lists, user info, file upload. Only Marketplace or internal apps.
blocker: Non-Marketplace distributed apps throttled to 1 req/min on history
notes: Search snippets say the Tier 1 limits were extended to existing installs of unlisted apps on 3 Mar 2026; the fetched changelog page (api.slack.com FAQ URL redirects to it) still says existing installs are unaffected, so verify. Developer sandboxes (docs.slack.dev/tools/developer-sandboxes): basic sandbox free for Developer Program members; full sandbox needs a paid workspace or payment method on file. Org-wide installs cannot use some bot scopes. A toolkit wanting full history access should plan for Marketplace listing.

one_liner: Cloud communications APIs for SMS, voice, WhatsApp, email, verification and video.
auth_notes: All REST requests use HTTP Basic: API Key SID + API Key secret (recommended; Main/Standard/Restricted key types, Standard keys cannot reach Accounts/Keys resources) or Account SID + Auth Token (needed for Accounts/subaccount endpoints). No end-user OAuth flow documented on the fetched page, so end users would supply Account SID + API key/secret. Separate test credentials exist.
access_notes: Free trial without credit card, expires 30 days after sign-up; product free units (e.g. 100 SMS, 100 WhatsApp, 75 voice minutes); only up to 5 verified recipients, sign-up country only, Twilio-provided content only, A2P 10DLC needs a paid account. Upgrading requires loading a balance and payment details (pay-as-you-go). Test credentials (no charges) work for Messages, Calls, IncomingPhoneNumbers and Lookup only.
api_breadth_notes: Twilio's MCP docs cite 1,800+ endpoints across 30+ products (Messaging, Voice, Verify, Conversations, Lookup, Studio, etc.).
mcp_notes: Two vendor servers: (1) hosted docs-only MCP at https://mcp.twilio.com/docs (Public Beta, no credentials, search/retrieve API specs, does not execute calls; OAuth-authenticated execution listed as planned); (2) twilio-labs/mcp (npm @twilio-alpha/mcp, 'Twilio Alpha'), local npx server exposing all public APIs, credentials ACCOUNT_SID/API_KEY:API_SECRET, filterable by --services/--tags.
notes: Sandbox = test credentials + magic numbers (https://www.twilio.com/docs/iam/test-credentials). Trial expiry and verified-recipient limits constrain live testing; production messaging to US numbers needs A2P 10DLC / toll-free verification. Fetch of /docs/iam/api/authentication returned 404; auth confirmed on requests-to-twilio page. Webhook request signing (X-Twilio-Signature) not covered on fetched pages. twilio-labs README also fetched (raw.githubusercontent.com/twilio-labs/mcp/main/README.md).

one_liner: Zoho's team chat app with channels, bots, calls and a Deluge-based developer platform.
auth_notes: Zoho OAuth 2.0: register client ID/secret, grant code -> access token (~1 h) + refresh token; header 'Authorization: Zoho-oauthtoken <token>'; per-endpoint scopes like ZohoCliq.Users.READ, ZohoCliq.Webhooks.CREATE, org-level scopes for bulk export. Data-center-specific domains (.com, .eu, .in, .com.au, .com.cn, .jp, .sa, .uk, zohocloud.ca). Messaging endpoints can also be called with a Cliq webhook token/authtoken.
access_notes: Cliq Free plan exists and the plan comparison lists 'API support: Yes' on Free, Standard, Professional and Enterprise. No overall usage cap; per-endpoint per-user throttles (e.g. 5-30 req/min) return 429. Bulk export (maintenance) endpoints are admin-only.
api_breadth_notes: ~20 resource groups: Users, Userfields, User Status, Departments, Roles, Designations, Remote Work, Chats, Channels, Threads, Teams, Messages, Scheduled Messages, Bots, Files, Calls & Meetings, Events, Reminders, Cliq Database, Bulk Export; likely 100+ endpoints (estimate, full page not read).
mcp_notes: Zoho Cliq MCP server, described by Zoho as official; created in the Zoho MCP console (mcp.zoho.com, regional variants) or Cliq Bots & Tools > Cliq MCP; remote, works with Claude, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf. Auth mechanism, tool count and plan requirements not stated on fetched pages (configure page says an 'appropriate plan' is needed).
notes: Toolkit must route accounts + API calls to the user's data center. Outgoing channel webhooks are deprecated (https://www.zoho.com/cliq/help/platform/channel-webhooks.html); Zoho recommends the Bot Participation Handler (Deluge) instead, so event triggers would need a Cliq bot that invokes an external URL rather than a native webhook subscription. Pricing page's 'API support' row was unreadable; confirmed via plan-comparison page. Free-plan platform object caps apply (e.g. 100 bots, 10 extensions per org).

one_liner: All-in-one collaboration suite (international Feishu): messenger, docs, Base, calendar, meetings, approvals.
auth_notes: App credentials (app_id/app_secret) exchanged for tenant_access_token (app identity, max 2 h); user_access_token via OAuth authorization code for user-identity calls. Custom (self-built) apps vs store (ISV) apps. Lark (larksuite.com) and Feishu (feishu.cn) apps/domains are not interchangeable.
access_notes: Developer console is self-serve; developers can debug with their own user_access_token before publishing and use free-review scopes immediately. Scopes take effect only after an app version is approved: custom apps need tenant-admin approval for review-required scopes; store apps need Lark Open Platform listing review plus tenant-admin install review, and advanced scopes are rejected without justification. Free Starter plan reportedly caps OpenAPI at 10,000 calls/month (search snippet of larksuite.com/plans; fetch returned no body).
api_breadth_notes: ~22 server-side product areas (Contacts, Messaging, Group chat, Cloud Docs, Calendar, Video Conferencing, Attendance, Approval, Bot, Tasks, Email, Admin, OKR, Minutes, Workplace, AI, Security & Compliance...) with hundreds of endpoints.
mcp_notes: larksuite/lark-openapi-mcp (npm @larksuiteoapi/lark-mcp), 'Feishu/Lark official OpenAPI MCP'; local npx, Beta. Uses app_id/app_secret, optional OAuth user login (--oauth, --token-mode user_access_token); preset tool bundles; no file upload or doc editing yet.
blocker: Store app listing review and tenant admin approval for scopes
notes: Lark doc pages are JS-rendered: the get-access-token page and larksuite.com/plans returned no body, so token lifetime comes from search results of the tenant_access_token_internal doc. Sandbox = test enterprise/test version where sensitive scopes are free-review. Events delivered by HTTP POST to a public URL (event subscriptions + callbacks). Feishu (China) is a separate platform; a toolkit should pick Lark international or support both domains. The 10k calls/month Starter quota would constrain testing on a free tenant; verify.

one_liner: Team chat app by CAKE.com with channels, DMs, threads and calls.
auth_notes: Pumble apps: consent link (clientId, scopes, redirectUrl) -> code exchanged at https://api-ga.pumble.com/oauth2/access for a user token plus bot token; tokens need no refresh, bot token is regenerated on reinstall; bot scopes prefixed 'bot:'. Alternatively the API addon issues per-user API keys (Api-Key/bearer header) for simple message/channel actions.
access_notes: API key addon is 'available on all plans' (incl. free) to Owners, Admins and Members; custom apps are created free in workspace settings or with pumble-cli. Installing an app in other workspaces requires publishing on CAKE.com Marketplace (public apps submitted for review) or a private app whitelisted to specific workspaces.
api_breadth_notes: Node SDK API client: 44 methods (26 messages incl. search/scheduled/drafts, 7 channels, 5 users, workspace, calls, app, files). API key addon: ~8 actions (send/reply/delete messages, reactions, create channel, list channels/messages).
mcp_notes: Pumble-hosted remote MCP at https://mcp.pumble.com/mcp; headers 'token' (user/bot token) and 'x-app-token' (App key) from a custom app; 19 tools (send/search/edit messages, channel messages, create channel, schedule message) gated by app scopes.
notes: Developer docs live on the CAKE-com GitHub Pages site (vendor org). Webhooks = app manifest eventSubscriptions to a URL (e.g. NEW_MESSAGE) per https://cake-com.github.io/pumble-node-sdk/manifest.html; the API-key addon has no Events API. API key rate limit up to 1000 req/min per user. MCP article is inconsistent on hostname (pumble.com vs mcp.pumble.com). Marketplace review criteria/timelines not found. API is narrower than Slack's (no admin/user management).

one_liner: Voice, video and text community chat platform organized into servers and channels.
auth_notes: OAuth2 authorization code (PKCE recommended for production), implicit (discouraged), client credentials. Bot authorization flow (scope=bot + permissions) adds the app's bot to a guild; most API calls then use the app's bot token ('Bot' auth scheme = other). User bearer-token scopes are limited (identify, email, guilds, connections...); dm_channels.read, rpc.*, voice etc. are partner-only and some scopes need Discord approval.
access_notes: Any developer creates an app and bot token free in the Developer Portal. Privileged intents (MESSAGE_CONTENT, GUILD_MEMBERS, GUILD_PRESENCES) can be self-enabled for apps under 10,000 users; above that, or once verification-eligible (100+ guilds), Discord review/verification is required or the Gateway closes with 4014.
api_breadth_notes: REST API over guilds, channels, messages, members, roles, webhooks, interactions/application commands, emojis, stickers, scheduled events, auto-moderation, etc. (100+ operations, estimate) plus the WebSocket Gateway for real-time events.
mcp_notes: No official action MCP server found; many community servers (e.g. SaseQ/discord-mcp, @discord-mcp/core). docs.discord.com/mcp answered GET with 405, consistent with a docs-search MCP endpoint that third parties describe; unverified and docs-only.
blocker: Privileged intents need Discord review above 10,000 users
notes: Bot must be invited to each guild; reading message text needs the MESSAGE_CONTENT intent. Real-time message events come via the Gateway WebSocket; HTTP webhook events (https://docs.discord.com/developers/events/webhook-events, Ed25519-signed) cover only app authorize/deauthorize, entitlements, lobby and game DMs. No separate sandbox; test in free servers. support-dev.discord.com privileged-intent article returned 403. Old discord.com/developers/docs URLs 301 to docs.discord.com.

one_liner: Cloud messaging app; Bot API lets bots message users, groups and channels.
auth_notes: Bot token from @BotFather embedded in the URL path (https://api.telegram.org/bot<token>/METHOD); no OAuth. Optional secret_token header to verify webhook deliveries. The MTProto client API (user accounts) is a separate surface, used by several community MCP servers.
access_notes: Anyone with a Telegram account creates a bot via @BotFather at no cost and with no review. Bots in groups run in privacy mode by default (see only relevant messages/commands unless admin).
api_breadth_notes: Bot API 10.5 lists ~190 methods (messages, media, chat admin, stickers, inline mode, payments, games, business, forum topics, webhooks); count from parsing method headings on the fetched page.
mcp_notes: No official Telegram MCP found; community servers include chigwell/telegram-mcp and sparfenyuk/mcp-telegram (MTProto user accounts) and Bot-API-based servers.
notes: Toolkit auth = user pastes their bot token (one bot per connection). getUpdates (long polling) and setWebhook are mutually exclusive; undelivered updates kept up to 24 h. Separate test environment (new account + bot, /test/ path). Official Bot API server limits uploads to 50 MB and downloads to 20 MB unless a Local Bot API server is self-hosted.

one_liner: Meta's WhatsApp Business Platform Cloud API for business messaging, templates and notifications.
auth_notes: Graph API bearer tokens: short-lived user tokens (testing), long-lived system user tokens (direct developers, need asset access to both WhatsApp and Messaging accounts), and Business Integration System User tokens per onboarded customer obtained by exchanging the Embedded Signup (Facebook Login for Business) code - the Tech Provider path.
access_notes: Meta developer app, test phone number and temporary token are self-serve and free; Standard Access covers testing by app admins/developers and a direct developer's own business without App Review. Serving other businesses needs Advanced Access to whatsapp_business_messaging and whatsapp_business_management via App Review (avg ~24 h, per-permission screencasts); search results also state business verification is required before App Review for Tech Providers.
api_breadth_notes: Messages, media, message templates, phone number registration, business profiles, WABA management, webhook subscriptions, flows, analytics (~50-100 operations, estimate).
mcp_notes: Meta-hosted remote 'WhatsApp Business Tools MCP' at https://mcp.facebook.com/whatsapp_business_tools, OAuth via Meta account: account discovery, phone number onboarding/registration, template management, webhook configuration, sending messages (launched ~Sept 2026). Companion Meta Social Technologies MCP at https://mcp.facebook.com/devtools.
blocker: App Review for Advanced Access to serve other businesses
notes: Free-form messages only within the 24-hour customer service window opened by a user reply; otherwise approved templates. Per-message pricing not fetched in this pass. Use the Cloud API; unofficial WhatsApp Web bridges carry ban risk. Docs are migrating from /docs/whatsapp to /documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp. Without Advanced Access, permissions don't appear in Embedded Signup and calls on non-owned accounts return error 200.

one_liner: Cloud phone system and AI voice platform for sales and support teams.
auth_notes: Basic auth with api_id:api_token generated in the Aircall dashboard (Integrations > API keys) for own-account use. OAuth2 authorization code (dashboard.aircall.io/oauth/authorize, POST api.aircall.io/v1/oauth/token) is required for public apps; an admin installs and the single token covers the whole company, limited to the phone numbers the admin selects.
access_notes: OAuth credentials and a developer account only after a Technology Partner application plus integration-plan review (1-5 business days). API keys need an Aircall customer account: no free plan (Essentials $30/license/mo, 3-license minimum; 'free access' trial offered, length unstated); 'APIs & webhooks' included on all plans, Messaging API not on Essentials. Aircall says public apps shouldn't ask users for API keys.
api_breadth_notes: 22 resource groups (Users v1/v2, Teams, Calls, Conversations, Numbers, Contacts, Tags, Webhooks, Messages, Dialer/Outbound Campaigns, Conversation Intelligence, AI Voice Agents, Analytics, ...), roughly 140-150 endpoints (estimate); 120 req/min per company.
mcp_notes: Aircall's MCP FAQ says they don't offer an MCP server yet. Third-party/community servers exist (Allo, StackOne, Zapier, Composio).
blocker: OAuth requires approved Aircall technology partnership
notes: 78 webhook event types (calls, messages, users, contacts, numbers, AI agents...). Approved partners get a 'developer account' (may serve as sandbox; not confirmed). Building/testing via Basic auth (https://developer.aircall.io/docs/basic-authentication) needs a paid or trial Aircall account. developer.aircall.io/api-references 301-redirects to developers.aircall.io.

one_liner: Communications APIs for SMS, voice, messaging channels, verification and video.
auth_notes: API key + secret via HTTP Basic (newer APIs; dual-secret rotation supported). JWT (RS256) signed with an Application's private key for Messages, Voice, Video and client SDKs; Basic on Messages/Verify lacks webhooks and ACLs. Signature secret used for signed messages. No end-user OAuth documented.
access_notes: Signup gives API key/secret, EUR 2 free test credit and DEMO mode (messages to up to 10 destination numbers, demo notice on SMS); exit demo mode by adding credit/payment method. Pay-per-request thereafter. Free Messages API Sandbox (WhatsApp, Viber, Messenger, Instagram; 100 msgs/month, 1 msg/s).
api_breadth_notes: Products include Messages, SMS, Voice, Verify, Video, Number Insight, Numbers, Account, Applications, Reports, etc. (100+ operations, estimate).
mcp_notes: Vonage Tooling MCP (@vonage/vonage-mcp-server-api-bindings): open source, local npx; env VONAGE_API_KEY/SECRET/APPLICATION_ID/PRIVATE_KEY64/VIRTUAL_NUMBER; tools balance, SMS, TTS outbound call, list applications/numbers, link number to app, WhatsApp/RCS. Hosted tooling server 'in progress'. Separate Documentation MCP (hosted, docs search).
notes: Messages apps need inbound and status webhook URLs. JWT flows require handling each user's application private key, so Basic key/secret is the simpler toolkit path where supported. Support article on trial test numbers (api.support.vonage.com) returned 403; support articles reportedly cite 5 test numbers, conflicting with the 10 on the Messages page. Sandbox page: https://developer.vonage.com/en/messages/concepts/messages-api-sandbox. MCP intro page: https://developer.vonage.com/en/mcp-server/conceptual-guides/introduction-to-vonage-mcp.
